accepted.s: The office of Whip in the Indian parliamentary system derives its authority primarily from:
o: The Rules of Procedure of Parliament
A specific provision of the Constitution
accepted.x: The office of Whip is not mentioned in the Constitution, the Rules of the House or any parliamentary statute. It is based on conventions of parliamentary government.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a conventional office from a constitutional, statutory or rule-based office.
accepted.sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding a party Whip:
1. Each political party appoints a Whip or Chief Whip.
2. The Whip seeks to ensure attendance and voting according to the party line.
3. Defiance of a Whip can attract disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. A party Whip enforces party discipline regarding attendance and voting, and defiance in relevant circumstances may attract disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.
accepted.tq: Check whether all statements describe connected functions and consequences of party discipline.
accepted.sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of Whip:

List-I (Type)
A. One-line Whip
B. Two-line Whip
C. Three-line Whip

List-II (Purpose)
1. Strict voting direction
2. Informative communication
3. Direction to attend the House

Select the correct code:
accepted.x: A one-line Whip is informative, a two-line Whip directs members to attend, and a three-line Whip gives a strict voting direction.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with swapped functions.
accepted.sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which Union Minister maintains close contact with the Chief Whips of political parties in both Houses of Parliament?
o: Minister of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
accepted.x: The Minister of Parliamentary Affairs keeps close contact with the Chief Whips of parties in both Houses.
accepted.tq: Use the functional association between parliamentary coordination and the concerned ministry.
accepted.sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to parliamentary committees, consider the following statements:
1. The Ethics Committee of the Rajya Sabha was constituted on 4 March 1997.
2. The Ethics Committee of the Lok Sabha was constituted on 16 May 2000.
3. The Committee on Empowerment of Women in both Houses was constituted on 29 April 1997.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three dates are correct: 4 March 1997 for the Rajya Sabha Ethics Committee, 16 May 2000 for the Lok Sabha Ethics Committee and 29 April 1997 for the Committee on Empowerment of Women.
accepted.tq: Separate closely spaced institutional dates before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the composition of the Committee of Privileges?
o: Lok Sabha—10 members nominated by the Chairman; Rajya Sabha—15 members nominated by the Speaker
Lok Sabha—15 members nominated by the Speaker; Rajya Sabha—10 members nominated by the Chairman
Both Houses—15 members elected by the respective Houses
Both Houses—10 members nominated by the President
accepted.x: The Lok Sabha Committee of Privileges has 15 members nominated by the Speaker, while the Rajya Sabha Committee has 10 members nominated by the Chairman.
accepted.tq: Check both membership and nominating authority; the two Houses are deliberately reversed in distractors.
accepted.sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is the ex-officio Chairperson of which of the following committees?
1. Business Advisory Committee
2. Rules Committee
3. General Purposes Committee

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Speaker is ex-officio Chairperson of the Business Advisory Committee, the Rules Committee and the General Purposes Committee.
accepted.tq: Identify the common constitutional-office relationship across the listed committees.
accepted.sec: Office of Whip - basis, functions, types  [APPSC]

accepted.s: An Adjournment Motion in Parliament can be admitted only when it concerns:
o: A demand for grant requiring reduction by one rupee
Any matter raised without prior notice
A matter of definite and urgent public importance
accepted.x: An Adjournment Motion sets aside the normal business of the House to discuss a definite matter of urgent public importance.
accepted.tq: Match the motion with its defining procedural condition rather than with a related device.
accepted.sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about an Adjournment Motion:
1. It can be moved only in the Lok Sabha.
2. It requires the support of 50 members.
3. It has an element of censure.
4. Its debate lasts at least two hours and thirty minutes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. An Adjournment Motion is a Lok Sabha device, requires 50 members' support, carries an element of censure and involves debate of at least two hours and thirty minutes.
accepted.tq: Test the House, numerical requirement, character and duration together.
accepted.sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following motions is available in both Houses and seeks an authoritative statement from a Minister?
accepted.x: A Calling Attention Motion is available in both Houses and seeks an authoritative statement from the concerned Minister.
accepted.tq: Use the combination of House availability and procedural purpose to identify the motion.
accepted.sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Calling Attention procedure is significant because it is:
o: An Indian innovation introduced in 1962 but not included in the Rules
An Indian innovation introduced in 1954 and included in the Rules of Procedure
accepted.x: Calling Attention is an Indian innovation dating from 1954 and is provided for in the Rules of Procedure.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the dates and rule status of Calling Attention and Zero Hour.
accepted.sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Privilege Motion — Rule 222 in the Lok Sabha
2. Privilege Motion — Rule 187 in the Rajya Sabha
3. Cut Motion — Demands for Grants
4. Calling Attention — Both Houses

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. Privilege matters are governed by Rule 222 in the Lok Sabha and Rule 187 in the Rajya Sabha; cut motions relate to demands for grants, while Calling Attention is available in both Houses.
accepted.tq: Verify each motion against both its procedural rule and its House or subject scope.
accepted.sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A motion concerning a breach of privilege by a Minister or a Member is governed by which of the following rules?
o: Rule 198 in the Lok Sabha and Rule 377 in the Rajya Sabha
Rule 222 in the Lok Sabha and Rule 187 in the Rajya Sabha
Rule 377 in the Lok Sabha and Rule 180A in the Rajya Sabha
Rule 184 in the Lok Sabha and Rule 193 in the Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: Privilege matters are governed by Rule 222 of the Lok Sabha and Rule 187 of the Rajya Sabha.
accepted.tq: Avoid rule-number swaps by associating the lower and upper Houses separately.
accepted.sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes a Censure Motion from a No-confidence Motion?
o: A No-confidence Motion may be moved in either House
Censure requires reasons to be stated, whereas No-confidence does not require reasons
Passing a Censure Motion necessarily forces the Council of Ministers to resign
Censure is directed only against the entire Council of Ministers, whereas No-confidence may target one Minister
accepted.x: A Censure Motion must state reasons, while a No-confidence Motion need not state reasons. Censure may target a Minister, a group or the whole Council, whereas No-confidence is against the entire Council in the Lok Sabha.
accepted.tq: Compare the requirement, target and consequence instead of relying on the names alone.
accepted.sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Censure Motion may be directed against a Minister, a group of Ministers or the whole Council of Ministers.
2. A No-confidence Motion is directed against the entire Council of Ministers.
3. Passing a Censure Motion compels the Council of Ministers to resign.
4. Passing a No-confidence Motion requires the Council of Ministers to resign.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is false because passing a Censure Motion does not compel resignation, whereas passing a No-confidence Motion does.
accepted.tq: Find the single reversed consequence in a comparison table.
accepted.sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A No-confidence Motion in the Lok Sabha is governed by which rule and requires the support of how many members for admission?
accepted.x: A No-confidence Motion is governed by Rule 198 of the Lok Sabha and requires the support of 50 members.
accepted.tq: Pair the correct rule number with the specific numerical threshold.
accepted.sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who decides whether a No-confidence Motion is in order and admits or rejects it?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
accepted.x: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha decides whether a No-confidence Motion is in order and admits or rejects it.
accepted.tq: Ask which presiding authority performs the procedural gatekeeping function.
accepted.sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the type of Cut Motion?
o: Policy Cut — reduction of the demand to Re 1
Economy Cut — reduction of the demand to Rs 100
Token Cut — reduction by an amount representing total rejection of policy
Policy Cut — reduction by a specified amount without expressing policy disapproval
accepted.x: A Policy Cut proposes reduction of the demand to Re 1 to express disapproval of the policy. An Economy Cut involves a specified reduction, while a Token Cut reduces the demand by Rs 100 to ventilate a specific grievance.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the three cut motions by the amount and purpose of reduction.
accepted.sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Cut Motions:
1. They are moved on demands for grants.
2. An Economy Cut proposes reduction by a specified amount.
3. A Token Cut proposes reduction by Rs 100 to indicate a specific grievance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Cut Motions relate to demands for grants and include policy, economy and token cuts with their respective forms of reduction.
accepted.tq: Use the common subject first, then verify the distinctive numerical feature of Token Cut.
accepted.sec: Motions - House, requirement; censure vs no-confidence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding parliamentary questions is correct?
o: An Unstarred Question receives an oral answer and permits supplementary questions
A Starred Question receives an oral answer and permits supplementary questions
A Starred Question receives a written answer and permits no supplementary question
Both Starred and Unstarred Questions necessarily receive oral answers
accepted.x: A Starred Question receives an oral answer and permits supplementary questions. An Unstarred Question receives a written answer and does not permit supplementary questions.
accepted.tq: Separate the paired devices through the answer mode and availability of supplementaries.
accepted.sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

accepted.s: A Short Notice Question is intended for a matter of urgent public importance and may be asked with:
accepted.x: A Short Notice Question concerns an urgent matter of public importance and is asked with less than 10 days' notice. It receives an oral answer.
accepted.tq: Identify the exceptional notice period attached to an urgent procedural device.
accepted.sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Question Hour is correct?
o: It is an unscheduled period during which Ministers are not required to respond
It is the last hour of every sitting and is devoted only to private members' business
It is the first hour of every sitting during which Ministers answer questions
It is available only when an Adjournment Motion is admitted
accepted.x: Question Hour is the first hour of every sitting. Ministers answer questions during this period, which enables members to seek information and exercise control over the executive.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a formally scheduled device from the unscheduled Zero Hour.
accepted.sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Zero Hour?
o: It precedes Question Hour and is confined to starred questions
It is a device available only in the Rajya Sabha
It is expressly provided in the Rules of Procedure and requires ministers to reply to every matter
It is the time after Question Hour, permits matters to be raised without prior notice, and is not provided in the Rules of Procedure
accepted.x: Zero Hour follows Question Hour, allows members to raise important matters without prior notice, does not bind Ministers to reply and is not included in the Rules of Procedure. It is an Indian innovation associated with 1962.
accepted.tq: Separate Zero Hour from Question Hour and Calling Attention by notice, rule status and ministerial response.
accepted.sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

accepted.s: The parliamentary device associated with matters that are not points of order and are raised under Rule 377 in the Lok Sabha is:
accepted.x: Rule 377 of the Lok Sabha permits members to raise matters that are not points of order. The corresponding device in the Rajya Sabha is known as Special Mentions.
accepted.tq: Match the exact rule number with the formal name used in the concerned House.
accepted.sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Rule 377, Lok Sabha — Matters not raisable under any other device
2. Special Mentions, Rajya Sabha — Equivalent device to Rule 377 matters
3. Rule 193, Lok Sabha — Short-duration discussion without voting
4. Rule 184, Lok Sabha — Discussion followed by voting

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. Rule 377 and Special Mentions serve corresponding purposes in the two Houses, while Rules 193 and 184 distinguish discussions without and with voting respectively.
accepted.tq: Start with rule-number pairs and then confirm the presence or absence of voting.
accepted.sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

accepted.s: A discussion under Rule 193 of the Lok Sabha is characterised by:
o: A reduction of a demand for grant to Re 1
No voting and a short-duration format
A compulsory vote at its conclusion
A requirement that the matter be a breach of privilege
accepted.x: Rule 193 provides for a short-duration discussion without voting. Rule 184, in contrast, provides for discussion followed by a vote.
accepted.tq: Use the voting consequence to distinguish Rules 193 and 184.
accepted.sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following parliamentary discussion devices in chronological order of their introduction or institutional association:
A. Calling Attention
B. Short-duration discussion
C. Zero Hour

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Short-duration discussion is an Indian innovation of 1953, Calling Attention dates from 1954, and Zero Hour is associated with 1962. Therefore, the correct order is B, A, C.
accepted.tq: Place the dated devices first and compare the closely spaced years 1953, 1954 and 1962.
accepted.sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

accepted.s:
A Short-duration Discussion in the Lok Sabha has which of the following features?
1. It is limited to a maximum of two hours.
2. It is an Indian innovation of 1953.
3. It necessarily ends with a formal vote.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because a short-duration discussion does not involve voting.
accepted.tq: Identify the duration and origin while rejecting the false voting consequence.
accepted.sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

accepted.s: A half-an-hour discussion is intended for:
o: A matter that can be raised only through a No-confidence Motion
A demand for grant requiring reduction by Rs 100
A matter already sufficiently debated but requiring factual elucidation
A breach of privilege requiring immediate suspension of the House
accepted.x: A half-an-hour discussion is held on a matter that has been sufficiently debated but requires further factual elucidation. It involves no formal motion or vote.
accepted.tq: Apply the purpose of the device to a scenario requiring clarification rather than a fresh decision.
accepted.sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Half-an-hour discussion — formal motion followed by voting
accepted.x: The fourth pair is incorrect. A half-an-hour discussion does not involve a formal motion or voting; it is meant for factual elucidation on a matter already debated.
accepted.tq: Find the procedural feature that contradicts the defining nature of the device.
accepted.sec: Rules of Procedure devices - rule numbers  [other exams]
